# Volume 3 — Chapter VIII Nell’s First Proposal

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

No pinky-yellow sunset or green twilight marked the quiet departure of the old year. Rather, its end arrived amid a wild, white bluster and blow. On that night, the storm-wind sped across the black hollows and frozen meadows, groaned around the eaves resembling a lost creature, and slammed the snow hard against the rattling panes.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0000 }

“Precisely the type of evening folks enjoy snuggling under their bedclothes and enumerating their blessings,” Nell remarked to Odette Pullen, who had arrived to pass the afternoon and remain until morning. However, once they were snuggled under their bedclothes, inside Nell’s small porch chamber, Odette was contemplating something other than her blessings.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0001 }

“Nell,” she stated in an exceedingly serious manner, “there is a matter I wish to share with you. Will you allow me”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0002 }

Following the previous evening's party hosted by Opal Pettigrew, Nell felt quite tired. Instead of hearing Odette’s disclosures, which she felt certain would prove uninteresting, she preferred by far to fall asleep. What lay ahead was something she had no intuitive forewarning of. Odette had likely become engaged as well; according to local gossip, Opal Pettigrew had agreed to marry the Tullyvale schoolteacher, a man over whom every girl was reportedly mad.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0003 }

“It won’t be long before I’m the sole unattached young woman remaining from our former group of four,” Nell mused, feeling sleepy. Speaking out loud, she uttered, “Of course.”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0004 }

“Nell,” Odette inquired, with even greater gravity, “how do you feel about my brother Barney?”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0005 }

This unlooked-for query caused Nell to draw her breath in sharply, her mind grasping about in vain. What was her opinion of Barney Pullen, for pity's sake? Round-faced, foolish, endlessly grinning, kindly Barney Pullen was someone she had never harbored a single thought about. Was Barney Pullen ever in anyone's thoughts?
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0006 }

“I—I fail to comprehend, Odette,” she faltered. “What are you trying to say—precisely?”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0007 }

“Is Barney to your liking?” Odette inquired directly.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0008 }

“Why—why—yes, I like him, of course,” gasped Nell, questioning whether she was speaking the absolute truth. Indubitably, Barney was not someone she disliked. Yet could her feeling of unconcerned tolerance toward him whenever he chanced to fall within her field of sight truly be counted as liking? What point was Odette attempting to make clear?
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0009 }

“Is it your wish to have him as a husband?” inquired Odette in a serene manner.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0010 }

“A husband!” Nell, who had been sitting up in bed to better contend with the issue of how she truly felt about Barney Pullen, now collapsed flatly onto her pillows, the breath completely knocked out of her. “Whose husband?”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0011 }

“Yours, naturally,” Odette replied. “Barney desires to make you his wife. He has perpetually been mad about you—and currently father has bestowed the upper farm upon him under his own name, so there is no obstacle to stop him from taking a bride. However, he is so bashful that he was unable to inquire directly whether you would take him, which led him to persuade me to act on his behalf. I would have preferred not to, but he harassed me incessantly until I promised that I would, provided a suitable opportunity arose. What is your opinion on the matter, Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0012 }

Could this be a dream? Was it akin to those horrific nightmares where you discover you are betrothed or wedded to a person you despise or are unacquainted with, having no clue how it occurred? No, she—Nell Harcourt—was resting right there, fully awake, inside her own bed, while Odette Pullen sat next to her, composedly making a marriage proposal on behalf of her brother Barney. Nell was uncertain if she felt like squirming or laughing; however, neither reaction was possible, because she had to avoid injuring Odette’s feelings.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0013 }

“I—I was unable to wed Bill, don't you see, Odette,” she succeeded in breathing out. “Indeed, a thought like that was never in my mind—not once!”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0014 }

“It probably didn't,” concurred Odette. “Courting is something Barney has constantly been much too timid to consider. Even so, you could reflect upon it, Nell. My brother Barney is a fine man, which I am obligated to state. He lacks any negative vices, works extremely hard, and is someone you can count on. ‘A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.’ He instructed me to inform you that he would be entirely agreeable to waiting until your college education is finished, should you demand it, even if his preference is a wedding this spring prior to the start of planting. I feel certain he would constantly treat you with great kindness, and, Nell, you are aware of how delighted I would be to gain you as a sister.”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0015 }

“I cannot marry Barney,” Nell stated firmly. Having regained her composure, she was now experiencing a touch of annoyance. The entire situation was utterly absurd. “It is pointless to consider it, Odette. My feelings for him are not of that nature, and you need to inform him of this.”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0016 }

“Indeed, I never anticipated your agreement,” Odette uttered with a weary exhale, believing she had given her utmost effort. “Though I informed Barney that requesting this of you seemed completely futile, he urged me anyway. So, Nell, your choice has been finalized, and I trust you will not rue it.”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0017 }

Odette’s tone was somewhat icy. It had been her firm conviction that the infatuated Barney stood zero prospect of persuading Nell into marriage. Even so, a slight bitterness touched her that Nell Harcourt, a person who was ultimately just a taken-in orphan lacking any family whatsoever, would reject her brother—a member of the Brierley Pullen. Ah well, self-importance occasionally precedes a collapse, Odette brooded darkly.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0018 }

Nell allowed a smile to cross her face in the dark at the thought of ever being sorry for failing to wed Barney Pullen.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0019 }

“I hope Barney won’t take it too hard,” she said kindly.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0020 }

Odette shifted as though she was flinging her head back against her pillow.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0021 }

“Oh, he won’t break his heart. Barney possesses far too much good sense for that to happen. He likes Nettie Scobie fairly well, too, and mother would prefer him to marry her over anyone else. She is a very capable manager and saver. I believe that as soon as Barney is certain you refuse to have him, he will choose Nettie. Please do not speak of this to anybody, will you, Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0022 }

“Certainly not,” said Nell, who lacked any wish at all to broadcast to the world that Barney Pullen sought her hand in marriage, choosing her, when everything was taken into account, over Nettie Scobie. Nettie Scobie!
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0023 }

“And now I think we should try to get some sleep,” Odette proposed.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0024 }

Slumber came effortlessly and promptly to Odette; yet, despite being extremely dissimilar to MacBeth in the majority of ways, she had undoubtedly managed to slay sleep for Nell. That proposed-to damsel remained upon an insomniac pillow until the wee sma’s, though her thoughts were distant from being romantic. Nevertheless, it was not before the following morning that she possessed a chance to enjoy a hearty laugh about the entire business. Once Odette had departed for home—bearing a trace of frost in her tone and demeanor still, owing to Nell having refused the distinction of a union with the House of Pullen so thanklessly and firmly—Nell withdrew to the porch room, closed the door, and finally enjoyed her full laugh.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0025 }

“If only there were someone to share this humor with!” was her thought. “However, that is impossible. Isolde is the sole person I would wish to confide in, yet, setting aside my oath of secrecy to Odette, I am unable to share anything with Isolde anymore. Every detail gets passed on to Gideon—of that I am certain. At any rate, my initial proposal of marriage has happened. While I anticipated its eventual arrival—it never occurred to me that it would arrive through an intermediary. Though it is immensely amusing—it nevertheless carries a certain sharp pain.”
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0026 }

Nell was fully aware of what made it hurt so much, even if she refrained from expressing it in words. She had cherished her own private fantasies regarding the initial occasion when a person might pose that momentous query to her. Furthermore, within those fantasies, the moment had invariably been immensely romantic and lovely: while the “some one” was required to be exceedingly handsome, dark-eyed, distinguished in appearance, and articulate, regardless of whether he turned out to be Prince Charming, destined to be overjoyed by a “yes,” or a suitor who had to receive a sorrowful, exquisitely phrased, yet firm rejection. In the case of the second option, the rejection was meant to be conveyed with such finesse that it would closely resemble an acceptance, whereupon he would depart, having kissed her hand, guaranteeing her his unchangeable, lifelong allegiance. Additionally, the event was bound to remain a lovely recollection, serving as a source of pride while carrying a slight tinge of sadness, too.
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0027 }

And at present, this exciting event had proven to be nothing more than ridiculous. Barney Pullen had coaxed his sister into making the offer on his behalf since he had been granted the upper farm by his father; and provided that Nell did not desire to “have him”, he could take Nettie Scobie instead. There was romanticism for you, indeed! Nell gave a laugh—and subsequently a sigh. The freshness had been wiped away from a single youthful fantasy. Was this distressing sequence destined to continue till all things turned ordinary and dull?
{: #nw-v03-c08-p0028 }
